notes: E-025, E-026 and E-029 support meaningful ConnectedCooking fleet adoption and workflow functionality. E-010 and E-030 correctly prevent free connectivity from being treated as disclosed SaaS economics, consistent with C-006.

E-013, E-014 and E-041 support broad route-to-market, demand-generation and certified-service mechanisms. E-015 and E-048 with C-004/C-012 correctly retain dealer dependence and undisclosed retained service economics, so the finding remains MIXED.

E-049, E-051 and E-054 establish credible competitor overlap across intelligence, connectivity and multifunctional cooking. C-011 and E-058/E-059 correctly prevent feature overlap or workflow familiarity from being converted into hard switching-cost proof.
E-005, E-047 and E-048 with C-005 support the recurring-economics weak link; the 31% non-appliance bucket is not classified as recurring revenue.
E-032, E-033 and E-038 with C-007 support the customer-ROI weak link: resource savings are evidenced more strongly than representative total payback.
C-001 is appropriately retained as a material denominator conflict, and the unresolved market-share question does not accept management's approximately 50% headline share as total-market share.
The output remains ASSIST-only and does not render a final moat, durability, runway, valuation, score, routing or investment conclusion.
